citation.title: Disruption Event Characterization and Forecasting in Tokamaks
citation.authors: S.A. Sabbagh, J.W. Berkery, Y.S. Park, J. Butt, J.D. Riquezes, et al.
citation.year: unknown (accepted manuscript; publication year not stated in supplied text)
citation.venue: Physics of Plasmas (inferred from AIP manuscript header; not confirmed in text)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1063/5.0133825 (stated on manuscript header as article DOI)

topic: Physics-based automated disruption event-chain characterization and forecasting (DECAF) on NSTX, MAST, and KSTAR databases.
own_question: Can automated event chains and physics or reduced models forecast disruptions early enough for avoidance or mitigation?
actual_method_and_evidence: Analysis is offline and uses non-real-time inputs. The work applies rule and point-based warning levels, including a 15-criterion MHD warning, a reduced kinetic RWM model fit to MISK, and an island power balance model using TRANSP profiles. It also produces disruptivity maps. Reported results are disruption-forecast statistics. Carbon CES rotation is named only as a generic DECAF input on KSTAR. There is no Ti nowcasting, no BES or ECEI use, and no comparison of temperature estimators. The text mentions an initial KSTAR real-time installation, but its results are not reported.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant: the targets are disruption events, not CES temperature reports. No report arrival-time analysis is given.
validation_if_relevant: Database-level true-positive and false-positive percentages for disruption prediction are reported. No train/test split is described.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite it as evidence of CES Ti nowcasting or of BES/ECEI value for ion temperature.
Do not claim real-time DECAF performance on KSTAR was demonstrated.
Do not treat the use of CES rotation as validation of CES temperature labels.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude, or at most give a brief optional-application mention of disruption forecasting. Its problem, targets, and diagnostics do not match our CES temperature nowcasting study.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
